title: Sum After Removing k Minimums
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of `n` integers and an integer `k`. Perform the following operation exactly `k` times: remove the smallest element of the array. If the smallest value occurs more than once, remove only one occurrence of it.

Return the sum of the elements that remain. If every element has been removed, the sum is `0`.

**Follow-up:** the problem was posed as a heap exercise. Can you explain the cost of doing it with a min-heap (`k` pops) compared with sorting the whole array, and when each one wins?
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers `nums[0] ... nums[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the sum of the remaining elements.

examples.explanation: The two smallest elements are 1 and 3. Removing them leaves 7, 9 and 4, whose sum is 20.
First remove -1, then two of the four 2s (one occurrence per operation). The remaining elements are 2, 2 and 5, so the sum is 9.
k equals n, so every element is removed and nothing is left to sum.

hints: Which elements end up removed? It only depends on the k smallest values, not on the order of the array.
Repeatedly extracting a minimum is exactly what a min-heap (priority queue) does; the sum of the rest is the total minus what you popped.
Sorting once and summing the suffix gives the same answer. Watch out for k = 0 and k = n, and use 64-bit sums.
